observations.explanation: The paper describes hierarchical localization, patch sampling, test filtering, and majority voting (pp. 3–6). Its repair ablation reports improvements from 70 fixes with a single sample, to 78 with multiple samples and majority voting, and 82 with test filtering (p. 8). “Reproducible-in-principle” is appropriately qualified; the reported component gains concern the repair setups.

On SWE-bench Lite, AGENTLESS reports 82/300 resolved at an average cost of $0.34 and describes its result as the highest among open-source approaches (pp. 6–7). The paper separately lists commercial and closed-source approaches and notes limits on verifying some results (p. 6).
The authors manually classify SWE-bench Lite problems, exclude 48 specified problematic problems to form a 252-problem subset, and report that the general ranking remains roughly the same (p. 10).

The implementation uses GPT-4o and the evaluation focuses on SWE-bench Lite (p. 6). Baseline results are taken from official leaderboards or papers/repositories, and the authors say most closed-source baselines provide no trajectories and cannot be verified in that respect (p. 6). The stated limits on generalization are consistent with this scope.
